propositions: The _DRIFT_WARNED set in outbound_mapper.py is a process-global dedupe cache that suppresses duplicate drift warnings, causing test order-dependency when multiple tests assert drift warnings are emitted.
Status-mapping tests do not reset _DRIFT_WARNED between test runs, allowing pollution from earlier tests to suppress expected warnings in later tests via the dedupe mechanism.
test_unmapped_status_drifts can fail if an earlier test has already recorded 'blocked' in _DRIFT_WARNED, because the dedupe suppresses the warning that the assertion expects to see on stderr.

An autouse pytest fixture calling outbound_mapper.reset_drift_warnings() before each test in test_status_mapping.py will isolate test state and eliminate order-dependency without changing production code.

A two-part oracle test can verify fixture effectiveness: the first part records 'blocked' in _DRIFT_WARNED, the second asserts the warning still fires only if the fixture cleared the set between them.
